description: The Executive LLM is a single LLM that generates responses for all AI teammates, has access to the pedagogical rubrics, and is prompted to \"create situations that will allow the subject to demonstrate their skill, so that their skill level can be quantitatively inferred\".
title: Executive LLM adaptive assessment method

description: The authors developed an SDL framework from a literature review of accreditation standards and guidelines across health professions education programs.
title: Expanded seven-step self-directed learning (SDL) framework for identifying SDL activities and assessment methods

description: The article describes an evidence-review approach in which a research organization compiles a large body of studies and convenes expert panels to interpret the data.
title: Expert-panel interpretation of compiled educational evidence

description: The framework is an LLM-based teacher assessment architecture in which trustworthiness and explainability are built into inference rather than appended afterward.
title: Explainable-by-design framework coupling dual-lens hierarchical attention, trust-gated inference, and on-the-spot explanation generation

description: This framework pairs a model explainer with unsupervised learning to reveal heterogeneity hidden by binary classification.
title: Explanation-aware clustering

description: EIRT is described as \"a special name given to models of multilevel, categorical responses, in which latent estimates are generated for both item and person parameters and explanatory variables can be modeled as predictors of responses across levels of analysis\".
title: Explanatory Item Response Theory (EIRT)

description: This principle holds that debates over alternative longitudinal models should distinguish defensible modeling choices from specification errors that depart from SEM logic.
title: Explicit assumption specification when comparing alternative longitudinal models

description: The review recommends that family medicine education research be explicitly theoretically informed, arguing that articulation of underlying assumptions is needed for researchers to critically engage with study findings.
title: Explicit theoretical-framework and epistemological-assumption specification in education research

description: Because disciplines frame inequality differently—some problematizing unequal outcomes, others unequal treatment or unequal provision—researchers should make their framing explicit.
title: Explicit theoretical-lens specification for educational-inequality research

description: The review organizes school-based creativity support into two branches.
title: Explicit vs. implicit interventions as a two-branch taxonomy of school-based creativity support

description: The article develops an exploratory, unsupervised methodology that applies clustering to university pre-admission data to find latent structures without predefined labels.
title: Exploratory unsupervised clustering methodology for identifying at-risk student profiles from pre-admission data

description: The ELSD model represents syntax acquisition as \"a simple exponential learning process\" in which grammatical proficiency grows with experience, with an experience discount factor modeled separately for simultaneous bilinguals, immigrants, and non-immersion learners.
title: Exponential Learning with Sigmoidal Decay (ELSD) model of syntax acquisition

description: The article applies an exponential random partition model to the formation of student teams in higher education.
title: Exponential random partition model for student team formation

description: The ESDM is the authors' alternative to the reciprocal effects model of academic self-concept and achievement.
title: Extended Skill Development Model (ESDM)

description: The paper extends Strobel et al.'s (2024) taxonomy of GenAI applications — originally derived from 100 commercial and professional applications — into a classification lens for educational settings.
title: Extended Strobel taxonomy of five student–GenAI entanglement types

description: The ETDP, described by Kundisch et al.
title: Extended Taxonomy Design Process (ETDP)
